geo = read.delim("riqueza.txt", header = T)

p = ggplot(geo, aes(x, y, size = N, colour = N))

Thank you very much in advance.

Best,

Manuel

have a closer look at this page:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/plotting-polygon-shapefiles

library(maptools)
library(ggplot2)

## read ?gpclibPermit carefully
## The licence for gpclib is not Free or
## Open Source and explicitly forbids
## commercial use. See library(help=gpclib).
## set Permit to TRUE
gpclibPermit()

myshp <- readShapeSpatial(system.file("shapes/sids.shp",
package="maptools"))

## Help ggplot2
## "To figure out the correct variable name for
## region, inspect as.data.frame(model)"

head(as.data.frame(myshp))

## OK, set region = CNTY_ID"
myshp.points <- fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(myshp,
region="CNTY_ID")

## Here you have long and lat
head(myshp.points)

shpm <- merge(myshp.points, myshp, by.x="id", by.y="CNTY_ID")
head(shpm)

p <- ggplot(shpm, aes(long,lat,group=group,fill=NWBIR74))
p <- p + geom_polygon() + geom_path(color="white") + coord_equal()
p

HTH
Patrick

parts:
Here's an example using a county boundary shapefile for Tennessee from the US census bureau....

I haven't checked this to see if it runs exactly as shown, but it was copied from the code that  produced the map here...
http://graunt.bus.utk.edu/news/

with a few minor edits and comments.


library(maptools)
library(rgdal)
library(ggplot2)

#Load in a shapefile, the original zip file containing this shapefile is at  http://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county.zip
county47 <- readShapeSpatial('~/Data/www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county/tl_2009_47_county.shp',   
#The original zip file containing this shapfile is at  http://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county.zip

# Define it's datum these were geographic coordinates...
proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD27"))
# Project to something cartesian.  The Tennessee state plane coordinate system seemed appropriate. 
# First define that projection, I' don't remember where I found these codes, but a google search found the CRS codes somewhere, sorry I can't be of more help on this now.
TNSP <- CRS("+init=epsg:2274")
# And Project...
county47 <- spTransform(county47,CRS=TNSP)

# Now turn that projected spatial dataframe into a database of x,y coordinates using fortify()
fortify.county <- fortify(county47,region='COUNTYFP')
# 'region' is the variable that uniquely identifies each feature (either a polygon ID, or a line ID)

# and plot...
pTN <- ggplot() + geom_path(aes(x=long,y=lat,group=id),data=fortify.county)

# I used geom_path this time, as I just wanted outlines, no fill.


Nicholas

library(maptools)
library(rgdal)
library(ggplot2)

#Load in a shapefile, the original zip file containing this shapefile is at  http://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county.zip
county47 <- readShapeSpatial('~/Data/www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county/tl_2009_47_county.shp',   
#The original zip file containing this shapfile is at  http://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2009/47_TENNESSEE/tl_2009_47_county.zip

# Define it's datum these were geographic coordinates...
proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD27"))
# Project to something cartesian.  The Tennessee state plane coordinate system seemed appropriate. 
# First define that projection, I' don't remember where I found these codes, but a google search found the CRS codes somewhere, sorry I can't be of more help on this now.
TNSP <- CRS("+init=epsg:2274")
# And Project...
county47 <- spTransform(county47,CRS=TNSP)

# Now turn that projected spatial dataframe into a database of x,y coordinates using fortify()
fortify.county <- fortify(county47,region='COUNTYFP')
# 'region' is the variable that uniquely identifies each feature (either a polygon ID, or a line ID)

# and plot...
pTN <- ggplot() + geom_path(aes(x=long,y=lat,group=id),data=fortify.county)

# I used geom_path this time, as I just wanted outlines, no fill.


Nicholas
